renderer.formatStyle: Date.ISO8601FormatStyle is UTC unless it is given one, so this is the UTC day whether or not that was the day meant, and in Utah the UTC day turns over at 5 pm in winter and 6 pm in summer: an evening run gets tomorrow. Say the zone: Date.ISO8601FormatStyle(timeZone: .current) when the local day is meant, or timeZone: .gmt when the UTC day is.
renderer.dateFormatter: ISO8601DateFormatter is UTC unless its timeZone is set, so this is the UTC day whether or not that was the day meant, and in Utah the UTC day turns over at 5 pm in winter and 6 pm in summer: an evening run gets tomorrow. Say the zone: set the formatter's timeZone to .current when the local day is meant, or to .gmt when the UTC day is.

isoStringCutToDate.text: This cuts [[timestamp]] down to its date part. [[why]] [[repair]]

why.TypeScript: `toISOString()` is always UTC, so the cut is the UTC calendar day whether or not that was the day meant, and in Utah the UTC day turns over at 5 pm in winter and 6 pm in summer: an evening run gets tomorrow.
why.Swift: ISO 8601 formatting is UTC unless it is given a time zone, so the cut is the UTC calendar day whether or not that was the day meant, and in Utah the UTC day turns over at 5 pm in winter and 6 pm in summer: an evening run gets tomorrow.

repair.TypeScript: Say the zone instead: `dateIso8601(date, 'UTC')` from `@nexus/source/time/FormatTime` when the UTC day is meant, or `dateIso8601(date, userTimeZone())` with `userTimeZone` from `@nexus/source/time/TimeZones` when the local day is meant.
repair.Swift: Format the day itself and say the zone: Date.ISO8601FormatStyle(timeZone: .current).year().month().day() when the local day is meant, or timeZone: .gmt when the UTC day is.

isoDateWithoutTimeZone.text: This formats a date as its ISO 8601 calendar day without naming a time zone. <<renderer>>
